## Do forecasts improve near resolution?

These data describe 800 resolved Manifold Markets questions and 43,694 daily
probability snapshots. The probability is the crowd's forecast that the answer
will be YES. Because Manifold uses play money, these results describe this
platform and dataset rather than prediction markets in general. The Parquet
files come from the [PPBDS r4ds-8 tutorial](https://github.com/PPBDS/misc.tutorials/tree/main/inst/tutorials/r4ds-8/data)
and were built from Manifold Markets' public API.

The absolute prediction error is the distance between a forecast and the
outcome (coded as 1 for YES and 0 for NO). The time buckets compare forecasts
made at different distances from resolution.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(arrow)

markets <- read_parquet("data/markets.parquet")
groups <- read_parquet("data/groups.parquet")
market_groups <- read_parquet("data/market_groups.parquet")

joined <- open_dataset("data/history.parquet") |>
  collect() |>
  left_join(markets, by = "market_id") |>
  mutate(
    outcome_numeric = if_else(outcome == "YES", 1, 0),
    prediction_error = abs(probability - outcome_numeric),
    days_to_resolution = as.numeric(
      as.Date(ymd_hms(resolved_at, tz = "UTC")) - date
    ),
    time_bucket = factor(
      case_when(
        days_to_resolution > 90 ~ "90+ days",
        days_to_resolution > 30 ~ "30–90 days",
        days_to_resolution > 7 ~ "7–30 days",
        days_to_resolution >= 1 ~ "1–7 days",
        days_to_resolution == 0 ~ "Final day"
      ),
      levels = c("90+ days", "30–90 days", "7–30 days", "1–7 days", "Final day"),
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )
```

### Accuracy by time horizon

The table gives the mean absolute error and the number of daily forecasts in
each time bucket. A smaller error means the forecasts were closer to the
eventual outcome.

```{r}
accuracy <- joined |>
  group_by(time_bucket) |>
  summarise(
    mean_error = mean(prediction_error),
    n_rows = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

accuracy |>
  transmute(
    `Time until resolution` = time_bucket,
    `Mean absolute error` = scales::percent(mean_error, accuracy = 0.1),
    `Daily forecasts` = n_rows
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
accuracy |>
  ggplot(aes(x = time_bucket, y = mean_error, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1, color = "#2166ac") +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#2166ac") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  labs(
    title = "Prediction markets get smarter near the deadline",
    subtitle = "Mean absolute error in Manifold Markets forecasts, by days remaining",
    x = "Days until resolution",
    y = "Mean absolute prediction error"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## How calibrated are final-day forecasts?

Calibration asks whether events assigned a given probability happen about that
often. The next chart shows the distribution of forecasts made on each
market's resolution day.

```{r}
final_day <- joined |>
  filter(days_to_resolution == 0)
```

```{r}
final_day |>
  ggplot(aes(x = probability)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "#2166ac", color = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of final-day forecasts",
    x = "Final-day probability of YES",
    y = "Number of markets"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

For the calibration table, forecasts are grouped into ten-percentage-point
bins. `Actual YES rate` is the share of markets in each bin that resolved YES;
the count shows how many markets support that estimate.

```{r}
calibration <- final_day |>
  mutate(prob_bin = round(probability * 10) / 10) |>
  group_by(prob_bin) |>
  summarise(
    actual_rate = mean(outcome_numeric),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

calibration |>
  transmute(
    `Forecast bin` = scales::percent(prob_bin),
    `Actual YES rate` = scales::percent(actual_rate, accuracy = 0.1),
    `Markets` = n
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
calibration |>
  ggplot(aes(x = prob_bin, y = actual_rate)) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray50"
  ) +
  geom_line(color = "#2166ac") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), color = "#2166ac", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Final-day forecasts are close to calibrated",
    subtitle = "The dashed line shows perfect calibration; point size shows market count",
    x = "Forecast probability of YES",
    y = "Observed share resolving YES",
    size = "Markets"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
